subject: Performance SLO & multi-region routing — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@finova.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finova.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / Performance targets + multi-region routing

Marissa — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so your team can size things out:

1) Latency targets: our product needs 95th percentile generation latency <= 250ms for the homepage search flow (short prompts, ~32 tokens). For longer async generation (reports ~400 tokens) we can tolerate p50 ~500ms and p95 ~1.2s.

2) Throughput / concurrency: we expect ~120 QPS peak for search endpoints with bursts to 300 QPS for 30–60s during marketing events. Concurrency per request is small (single prompt) but we need sustained concurrency of ~200 concurrent sessions for 24hr windows.

3) Streaming: we need server-side streaming for the report editor UI (partial tokens as they arrive). Low initial token latency is important — we lose UX if first bytes are >150ms.

4) Regional routing / residency: primary customers in the US and EU. EU customers require data residency (request and payloads must remain in EU). APAC is smaller now but we want a pathway for APAC routing with similar latency targets in the future.

5) Security/compliance: we will need confirmation of customer-managed keys or KMS integration for EU keys during the pilot.

Can your team provide:
- a short doc with expected p50/p95 numbers and recommended instance shapes for the above workload
- proposed routing plan: US-only vs EU-only endpoints, and a multi-region failover behavior for bursts

Happy to loop in procurement once we have a ballpark estimate (monthly committed capacity + burst).

Thanks — Tom

--
Tom Sanders
Head of Platform Product
Finova

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@finova.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / Performance targets + multi-region routing

Tom / Marissa — quick technical note after reviewing the call notes and Finova traffic profile. High level answers and assumptions below; happy to expand on any point in the deep-dive.

Assumptions: average prompt length for search = 32 tokens, generation length = 20 tokens; model footprint tested = open-llama-13b/quantized variant; batchable search requests (stateless) vs long-context report generation (stateful KV cache).

Recommended SLOs and target numbers (ballpark):
- Search (short prompts, streaming enabled): p50 ~45–70ms, p95 ~160–240ms when served on g5.2xlarge-equivalent dedicated instances with continuous batching and 200 QPS sustained across pool. First-byte streaming can be <100ms with small batching disabled for low-latency route.
- Report generation (400 tokens, streaming): p50 ~420–600ms, p95 ~900ms–1.5s depending on model and quantization. For consistent p95 <1.2s we recommend reserved pools on g5.8x-equivalent with concurrency sharding and warm KV cache.
- Throughput/burst: autoscaling pools with pre-warmed burst nodes can absorb short spikes to 300 QPS; recommend reserved capacity for baseline (commit to ~150 QPS equivalent) + burst buckets for marketing events.

Routing/data residency:
- EU residency: we can provision EU-only private pools where both inference and logs/embeddings remain in-region. For request payloads and transient model context we can enforce ingress egress rules and separate control plane flows; this meets strict residency but requires a dedicated EU pool.
- Multi-region failover: primary-region routing with low-latency preference; configured fallback to cross-region model variants (with a note that cross-region failover will increase p95 by ~200–400ms). We can make failover only for non-PHI/non-sensitive traffic if you require strict residency.

Streaming constraints and trade-offs: small-batch/no-batch low-latency route gives best first-byte times but reduces throughput efficiency; we suggest a hybrid route: low-latency lane (bounded concurrency, no batching) for homepage search, and high-throughput lane (aggressive batching) for background report generation.

Next: I’ll attach a short CSV with sample latency curves from benchmarking and a one-page SLO table for your review.

- Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: latency-results-20261001.csv (stub)

Thanks Aditya — useful numbers. A couple quick clarifications:

- The EU residency requirement applies to all request payloads and transient context for any EU customer (we cannot permit cross-border model execution for EU-customer requests).
- For APAC, we do not need immediate residency but would like a target p95 <= 300ms for search when APAC routing is live.

Can you confirm whether the dedicated EU pool will also support customer-managed KMS (we need that for encryption-at-rest of logs and embeddings)? If yes, we can fast-track an NDA and pilot.

Also please include an estimate of monthly committed cost for the recommended reserved pool sizes (baseline + burst). Looking to get procurement started.

Tom
